episodes.191951: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment. A few trees were blown down.
episodes.192014: A hot and humid air mass combined with an approaching cold front helped to produce scattered severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia. Thunderstorm winds blew down a considerable number of trees and power lines. The winds also knocked down a carport in Buckingham County.
episodes.192033: A favorable placement of the monsoon high over NM and then shifting to the west allowed for an influx of moisture and instability over the state of NM. Daily rounds of of showers and storms starting over the higher terrain midday spreading to lower elevation in the evening before slowly dissipating overnight each day. There were several reports of flash flooding over portions of central NM and a few severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.192159: West-southwesterly flow over Central Alabama with ample moisture return and DCAPE values exceeding 800 J/kg resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few of the storms were intense enough to produce isolated areas of damage, notably in Talladega County on July 17 and Elmore and Tuscaloosa counties on July 18.
episodes.192204: The synoptic pattern largely remained ridge-dominant continuing on through mid July, but sufficient moisture helped trigger isolated diurnal convection which produced a small number of strong wind gusts across Utah.
episodes.192409: Pulse thunderstorms developed in strong to extreme instability and moisture content, one of which turned severe.
episodes.192433: A cold front interacting with a hot and humid airmass produced a few loosely organized clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms. Localized wind damage was the main result in the wake of the storms.
episodes.192441: A cold front triggered bands of thunderstorms which produced gale force wind gusts over portions of the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192611: A cold front approached from the west on the afternoon of July 18th. Out ahead of this front, isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and tracked eastwards across the Alligator River, Croatan and Roanoke Sounds, and coastal waters north of Oregon Inlet. Some of these storms became strong in nature producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.192764: High pressure system situated over the four corners created the monsoonal patterns that brought in more moisture to help produce isolated/dry thunderstorms as PWAT values and instability was elevated.
episodes.193046: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment.  A few storms produced gusty winds with isolated impacts.  In addition, there was one fatality due to a lightning strike in Gadsden county.
episodes.193108: An approaching cold front and trough produced thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening on July 17th that resulted in localized flash flooding in northern New Jersey. MUCAPE values of 1000-2000 J/kg and PWATs of 2-2.2 inches allowed the thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall rates of 1-2 per hour. The thunderstorms produced rainfall totals of 1 to 2.5 inches.
episodes.193182: An isolated strong thunderstorm developed in southeast Wyoming during the afternoon of the 18th with penny size hail.
episodes.193192: Prevailing SW flow forced the sea breeze merger toward the Atlantic coast in the afternoon and evening where a few strong to severe storms produced gusty winds and some wind damage.
episodes.193193: Prevailing SW flow forced the sea breeze merger toward the Atlantic coast in the afternoon and evening where a few strong to severe storms produced gusty winds and some wind damage.
episodes.193386: A cold front over the Ohio Valley tracked south and east into portions of eastern Tennessee, western North Carolina and south central Virginia during the late evening and overnight. Scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of the front in the afternoon and evening hours. A more concentrated area of storms tracked southeast out of central Virginia, and led to isolated damaging winds and tree damage across Person and Vance Counties.
episodes.193387: A cold front draped northeast to southwest over Virginia and eastern Tennessee moved south and through central North Carolina in the late evening hours. A line of scattered to numerous showers and storms tracked southeastward ahead of the front during the afternoon and evening hours. Numerous downed trees and powerlines were reported, as well as some isolated flash flooding across Wake and Durham Counties.
episodes.193463: A weak surface boundary pushed slowly eastward on July 18. With unstable air ahead of the front, strong thunderstorms became numerous by the afternoon hours. Some of these became severe, with downbursts primarily causing wind damage.
episodes.193793: A weakening upper-level trough over the Florida Peninsula created an atmosphere that was conducive for diurnal convection as showers and storms developed along sea-breeze boundaries.
episodes.194027: Thunderstorms developed across east Colorado during the afternoon hours producing penny size hail in Cheyenne county and pea to nickel size hail in Yuma county.
episodes.194028: Thunderstorms developed across western Kansas during the afternoon hours which led to dime to nickel size hail in Sharon Springs along with a 63 mph wind gust in Sherman county.
episodes.194327: An upper level disturbance dropping south through the Plains along with a weak cold front kicked off a round of showers and thunderstorms across North Texas the afternoon of July 17. A few storms produced microbursts and minor wind damage.
episodes.194361: Torrential rainfall in Southwest Illinois on July 16th resulted in water levels at Thebes briefly returning to minor flood, with limited impacts to low-lying agricultural areas.
episodes.194362: Torrential rainfall in Southwest Illinois on July 16th resulted in water levels at Thebes briefly returning to minor flood, with limited impacts to low-lying agricultural areas.

episodes.194535: Heavy rain in Mid July led to river flooding on the White River basin.
episodes.194568: Strong storms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.194655: A couple thunderstorms embedded within a line along a cold front were able to become strong to severe east of I85. Microburst wind damage was able to bring down several trees.
episodes.194683: An upper low meandered over the region allowind scattered afternoon thunderstorm to develop. A couple became severe.
episodes.194750: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.194751: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of south central Virginia.

episodes.194966: Monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over southern Nevada. High winds, small hail, and minor flooding occurred in Henderson.
episodes.195023: A humid airmass and a stationary front draped over the area contributed to localized flash flooding near Pound.
episodes.195032: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. The pre-frontal trough moved into an area with high instability (1750-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE). This combined with Effect Bulk Shear values around 25 kt allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop. The storms were able to produce damaging wind gusts across southern CT, with DCAPE values around 750-1000 J/kg.
episodes.195033: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. episodes.195035: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. episodes.195066: A cluster of thunderstorms initiated across south-central Louisiana in response to high instability. This cluster of thunderstorms moved eastward while interacting with mid-level dry air. That dry air helped produced severe downdraft winds as the cluster moved through southeast Louisiana, southern Mississippi, and the adjacent marine areas. This complex also produced heavy rain in New Orleans which led to some flash flooding.

episodes.195074: A weak frontal boundary pushed though Central New Hampshire during the afternoon hours of July 17th, sparking numerous showers and thunderstorms. A weak shear environment prevented most storms from becoming severe, but a few isolated pulse severe thunderstorms were able to develop.
episodes.195091: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona with light steering winds brought locally heavy rain to parts of the area.
episodes.195199: A cold front approached with a hot and humid airmass in place. The result was several strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts across portions of New Jersey.
